prop:selection-rule-anchors-c1-c3:
Proposition Per-component selection rule \frac{1}{c+1}\sum_{\lambda\vdash c+1} \dim_q V_\lambda at c=1, c=3. Let q \in \mathbb{R}_{>0} and let h := q - q^{-1}. The per-component selection rule

  \mathrm{lw}(c)(q) \;:=\; \frac{1}{c+1} \sum_{\lambda \vdash (c+1)} \dim_q V_\lambda

satisfies the two exact identities:

  \mathrm{lw}(1)(q) \;=\; 1 \qquad (\text{exactly, } \forall q > 0),
  \mathrm{lw}(3)(q) \;=\; \frac{3q^2 + 4 + 3q^{-2}}{4} \;=\; \frac{5}{2} + \frac{3}{4} h^2.

These form the muon (c=1, knot) and the proton (c=3, Borromean 3-link) anchors of the per-component selection rule.

Significance

The zero-parameter selection rule reads \mathrm{lw}(L) = \frac{1}{c+1}\sum_{\lambda\vdash(c+1)} \dim_q V_\lambda, where c is the number of link components. The c=1 case equals 1 for all q (muon, a single-component knot with \mathrm{lw} = 1), and the c=3 case equals the Family-A formula \frac{5}{2} + \frac{3}{4}h^2 (proton, a three-component Borromean link). This proposition derives both identities directly from the hook-length formula: the sums run over the partitions of 2 and 4, and each \dim_q V_\lambda is [n]_q! divided by the product of the hook q-integers of \lambda.

Proof structure

The proof consists of two purely algebraic identities at the symbolic level:

  1. c=1 anchor: \frac{1}{2}\bigl( \dim_q V_{(2)} + \dim_q V_{(1,1)} \bigr) = 1. Both q-dimensions equal 1 (each partition of 2 has a hook product equal to the q-factorial), so the average is exactly 1.

  2. c=3 anchor: \frac{1}{4} \bigl( \dim_q V_{(4)} + \dim_q V_{(3,1)} + \dim_q V_{(2,2)} + \dim_q V_{(2,1,1)} + \dim_q V_{(1,1,1,1)} \bigr) = (3q^2 + 4 + 3q^{-2})/4.

    Using the explicit q-hook formula:

    • \dim_q V_{(4)} = \dim_q V_{(1,1,1,1)} = 1
    • \dim_q V_{(3,1)} = \dim_q V_{(2,1,1)} = [3]_q = q^2 + 1 + q^{-2}
    • \dim_q V_{(2,2)} = [4]_q / [2]_q = q^2 + q^{-2}

    Their sum is 1 + (q^2{+}1{+}q^{-2}) + (q^2{+}q^{-2}) + (q^2{+}1{+}q^{-2}) + 1 = 4 + 3q^2 + 3q^{-2}. Dividing by 4 yields the stated form. The h^2 form follows from q^2 + q^{-2} = h^2 + 2.

    Both steps operate as pure polynomial identities in \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]. They hold once the q^{-1} denominators are cleared.

q-usage discipline

This holds over real q > 0 (the aether-anchor regime). Both identities are q-rational, fibre-level constructs. The c=1 case holds for ALL q > 0 (an infinite set of constraints, not a single point).

Cross-references

  • Coulomb charge of a knot composite — introduces the h = q - q^{-1} structure at the per-crossing level.
  • Coulomb/strong ratio \tanh(\ln q) is the q-rational (q^2-1)/(q^2+1) — companion identity proving \tanh(\ln q) = (q^2-1)/(q^2+1) over real q > 0.
prop:selection-rule-c2-prediction:
Proposition Per-component selection rule at c=2: \mathrm{lw}(2) = (q+1)^2/(3q). Let q \in \mathbb{R}_{>0}. The per-component selection rule (Per-component selection rule \frac{1}{c+1}\sum_{\lambda\vdash c+1} \dim_q V_\lambda at c=1, c=3) applied at c=2 yields the closed form:

  \mathrm{lw}(2)(q) \;:=\; \frac{1}{3} \sum_{\lambda \vdash 3} \dim_q V_\lambda
  \;=\; \frac{2 + [2]_q}{3} \;=\; \frac{(q+1)^2}{3q}.

This supplies the rule's prediction for a 2-component link (e.g. the Hopf link). The closed form is a finite Laurent rational over \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]. Like the c=1 and c=3 anchors, it is derivation-tight (no fit, zero free parameters).

Significance

The per-component rule states \mathrm{lw}(c) = (1/(c+1)) \sum_{\lambda \vdash (c+1)} \dim_q V_\lambda. It is anchored at c=1 (muon, \mathrm{lw}=1 exactly \forall q) and c=3 (proton, \mathrm{lw} = 5/2 + (3/4)h^2 via Family-A). The c=2 case provides the first testable prediction of the rule beyond the two known anchors.

This proposition derives the closed form for c=2 from the hook-length formula itself: the sum runs over the three partitions of 3, with \dim_q V_{(2,1)} = [2]_q derived from the hook multiset \{3,1,1\} rather than asserted. Its anchors are derived the same way. Any independent determination of a 2-component link's linking_weight—such as a Hopf-link or gluon EM-linking application—can be tested against this exact formula.

Proof structure

The proof rests on a single algebraic identity at the symbolic level:

  \frac{1}{3} \bigl( \dim_q V_{(3)} + \dim_q V_{(2,1)} + \dim_q V_{(1,1,1)} \bigr)
  \;=\; \frac{(q+1)^2}{3q}.

Using the explicit q-hook values for partitions of 3:

  • \dim_q V_{(3)} = 1 (single-row Young diagram, all hooks contribute trivially)
  • \dim_q V_{(2,1)} = [2]_q = q + q^{-1} (standard rep at H_3; q-hook computation)
  • \dim_q V_{(1,1,1)} = 1 (single-column, conjugate of V_{(3)})

Their sum is 2 + q + q^{-1}. Dividing by 3 yields (2 + q + q^{-1})/3 = (q^2 + 2q + 1)/(3q) = (q+1)^2/(3q).

This constitutes a pure polynomial-ring identity over \mathbb{R}_{>0} once the q^{-1} denominators are cleared.

q-usage discipline

This holds over real q > 0 (aether-anchor regime). The closed form (q+1)^2/(3q) is a Laurent rational in \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}] — a fibre-level construction. At q = q_0, it evaluates to \approx 1.337. There is no |q|=1 step; both q and q^{-1} are real positive at any real q > 0.

Cross-references

  • Per-component selection rule \frac{1}{c+1}\sum_{\lambda\vdash c+1} \dim_q V_\lambda at c=1, c=3 — the two known anchors that establish the rule's existence.
sec:braiding-relations-intro: The categorical axioms of a quantum observable universe impose polynomial relations on the Iwahori–Hecke generators beyond the bare braid and quadratic relations, acting as a cohomological spectral filter on candidate closed braids.
rem:skein-archimedean-shadow: Remark Skein relations as an archimedean shadow. In the archimedean realisation, the Markov trace on the braid-group representation yields the Jones polynomial. The Skein relation corresponds to the trace of the characteristic equation of the braiding c_{V,V} (R-matrix braiding). Over \mathbb{Q}_\mathfrak{p}, the same characteristic equation holds (because the eigenvalues q and -q^{-1} are elements of the base ring), but no ambient 3-manifold exists in which to interpret it as a knot invariant. The categorical formulation of the braid action on tensor products therefore captures the algebraic content of braiding without presupposing an archimedean topology.
prop:vertex-algebra-relations:
Proposition QU and QUO axioms as relations on Hecke generators. The vertex operator algebra (V, Y, |0\rangle) inherits every QU and QUO axiom as a relation on the Hecke generators \sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_{n-1} of H_n(R, q), translated into knot coordinates: braid words in \sigma_i, the affine coordinate z on \mathcal{S}_p, the Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M, and cup/cap morphisms \cup\colon \mathbf{1} \to V^{\vee} \otimes V, \cap\colon V \otimes V^{\vee} \to \mathbf{1}. The generators obey the Hecke relation

  \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1 \qquad (1 \leq i \leq n-1),

and the vertex algebra of a QUO is the quotient of the free algebra on \{\sigma_i, \cup, \cap, L_{-1}, \mathrm{tr}_M, d, d_q, \star\} by 25 relations — 13 structural (the QU/QUO axioms QU-1 through QUO-4, with QUO-3a withdrawn) and 12 cohomological (C-1 through C-10) — catalogued in Table 2 and Table 3, coupled with the Hecke--Skein dictionary \sigma_i \leftrightarrow L_+, \sigma_i^{-1} \leftrightarrow L_-, 1 \leftrightarrow L_0.

Proof

Each axiom is translated into knot coordinates below.

QU Axioms (Quantum Universe)

QOU-1: Rigid braided monoidal structure (rigidity is a quantum-observable-universe condition; a quantum universe is braided but not rigid)

The braiding c_{V,V} acts on V^{\otimes n} via the Hecke representation \rho_n\colon B_n \to H_n(R, q). Write \sigma_i both for the braid generator in B_n and for its image \rho_n(\sigma_i) in H_n(R, q). Three families of relations encode rigidity and braiding:

(QU-1a) Hecke relation (quadratic):

  \sigma_i^2 =  (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1
  \qquad (1 \leq i \leq n-1).

Equivalently, (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0. The eigenvalues q (symmetric/bosonic channel) and -q^{-1} (antisymmetric/fermionic channel) correspond to the two OPE channels of the vertex algebra.

(QU-1b) Yang--Baxter relation (braid relation):

  \sigma_i \sigma_{i+1} \sigma_i
  = 
  \sigma_{i+1} \sigma_i \sigma_{i+1}
  \qquad (1 \leq i \leq n-2).

This is the hexagon axiom of the braided monoidal category, expressed in the Hecke basis.

(QU-1c) Far-commutativity:

  \sigma_i \sigma_j =  \sigma_j \sigma_i
  \qquad (|i - j| \geq 2).

Strands that do not share a crossing commute. This encodes the locality of the vertex algebra OPE.

(QU-1d) Snake identities (rigidity):

The cup \cup\colon \mathbf{1} \to V^{\vee} \otimes V and cap \cap\colon V \otimes V^{\vee} \to \mathbf{1} satisfy:

  (\cap \otimes \mathrm{id}_V) \circ
  (\mathrm{id}_V \otimes \cup)
  =  \mathrm{id}_V,
  (\mathrm{id}_{V^{\vee}} \otimes \cap) \circ
  (\cup \otimes \mathrm{id}_{V^{\vee}})
  =  \mathrm{id}_{V^{\vee}}.

In the graphical calculus, these are the zig-zag straightenings. In knot coordinates, \cup and \cap are the Markov-trace cup/cap insertions: the contour-integral endpoints of Y(a, z) around the Reeb fibre.

QU-2: Frobenius--Hopf relations

The operations multiplication \mu, comultiplication \Delta, unit \eta, counit \varepsilon, antipode S, and Frobenius form \int_A act on braid closures:

(QU-2a) Associativity:

  \mu \circ (\mu \otimes \mathrm{id})
  = 
  \mu \circ (\mathrm{id} \otimes \mu)
  \colon A^{\otimes 3} \to A.

In knot coordinates: merging three strands is independent of grouping. For braid words \beta_1, \beta_2, \beta_3:

  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(
    \rho(\beta_1 \cdot \beta_2) \cdot \rho(\beta_3)
  \bigr)
  = 
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(
    \rho(\beta_1) \cdot \rho(\beta_2 \cdot \beta_3)
  \bigr).

(QU-2b) Frobenius relation (sliding):

  (\mu \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ
  (\mathrm{id} \otimes \Delta)
  = 
  \Delta \circ \mu
  = 
  (\mathrm{id} \otimes \mu) \circ
  (\Delta \otimes \mathrm{id}).

In knot coordinates, this constitutes the saddle-point relation: a strand merge followed by a split equals a split followed by a merge. Graphically, this is the genus-0 cobordism identity: composing a pair of pants either way yields the same surface.

(QU-2c) Non-degenerate Frobenius pairing (A \cong A^{\vee}):

The Frobenius pairing \int_A \circ \mu\colon A \otimes A \to \mathbf{1} defines the Markov trace of the product:

  \langle a, b \rangle_F
  = 
  \int_A \mu(a \otimes b)
  = 
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\rho(\hat{\beta}_a \cdot \hat{\beta}_b)\bigr),

where \hat{\beta}_a is the braid word representing state a. Non-degeneracy requires that for every nonzero braid word \beta, there exists a \beta' such that \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta \cdot \beta')) \neq 0.

(QU-2d) Hopf (antipode) relation:

  \mu \circ (S \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta
  = 
  \eta \circ \varepsilon
  = 
  \mu \circ (\mathrm{id} \otimes S) \circ \Delta.

In knot coordinates, the antipode S is the braid reversal (orientation reversal of all crossings):

  S(\sigma_i) =  \sigma_i^{-1}
  =  \sigma_i - (q - q^{-1})
  \qquad\text{(from the Hecke relation)}.

The Hopf relation states that closing a braid word against its reverse yields the unknot (vacuum):

  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(
    \rho(\beta) \cdot \rho(\beta^{-1})
  \bigr)
  = 
  \mathrm{tr}_M(1)
  = 
  J_{0_1}(q).

(QU-2e) Coassociativity and counit:

  (\Delta \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta
  = 
  (\mathrm{id} \otimes \Delta) \circ \Delta,
  \qquad
  (\varepsilon \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta
  = 
  \mathrm{id}
  = 
  (\mathrm{id} \otimes \varepsilon) \circ \Delta.

In knot coordinates: splitting a strand into three is independent of grouping. The counit (trace evaluation at the unknot) acts as the unit for splitting.

QU-3: Fibre functor (Markov trace)

The fibre functor \tau\colon \mathbf{C} \to R\text{-Mod} realises the Jones--Markov trace (Jones--Markov trace). Its defining relation on Hecke generators is:

(QU-3a) Markov property I (conjugation invariance):

  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\sigma_i \cdot w\bigr)
  = 
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(w \cdot \sigma_i\bigr)
  \qquad \forall w \in H_n(R, q).

(QU-3b) Markov property II (stabilisation):

  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(w \cdot \sigma_n\bigr)
  = 
  z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(w),
  \qquad
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(w \cdot \sigma_n^{-1}\bigr)
  = 
  z_-\,\mathrm{tr}_M(w)
  \qquad \text{for } w \in H_n(R, q) \subset H_{n+1}(R, q),

where z = \dfrac{q^3}{q^2 + 1} is the Markov parameter on positive crossings and z_- = z - (q - q^{-1}) = \dfrac{1}{q(q^2 + 1)} is the induced weight on negative crossings.

(QU-3c) Quotient faithfulness:

  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\rho(\beta) \cdot w'\bigr) = 0
   \;\;\forall w' \in H_n(R, q)
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  \rho(\beta) \in \mathrm{rad}\,\mathrm{tr}_M.

At z = q^3/(q^2 + 1), the trace radical \mathrm{rad}\,\mathrm{tr}_M \subset H_n(R, q) vanishes for n \leq 2 and is spanned for n \geq 3 by the Wedderburn blocks of Young diagrams with at least three rows, so \mathrm{tr}_M descends faithfully to the Temperley--Lieb quotient \mathrm{TL}_n(q) \cong H_n(R, q)/\mathrm{rad}\,\mathrm{tr}_M of rank C_n = \frac{1}{n+1}\binom{2n}{n}.

QU-4: Differential calculus (translation operator)

The Kähler differentials \Omega^1(A) in the vertex algebra are generated by the translation operator L_{-1} = j (jet prolongation):

(QU-4a) Translation relation:

  [L_{-1}, Y(a, z)]
  = 
  \partial_z Y(a, z)
  = 
  Y(L_{-1} a, z).

In Hecke generators, the mode expansion yields:

  [L_{-1}, a_m] =  -m a_{m-1},

where a_m = \mathrm{tr}_M(\check{R}_{(a)} z^m) is the m-th mode of the vertex operator.

(QU-4b) Vacuum axiom:

  Y(|0\rangle, z) =  \mathrm{id}_V, \qquad
  L_{-1}|0\rangle =  0.

The unknot (|0\rangle = 1 \in A_0) produces the identity operator; translation annihilates the vacuum.

QUO Axioms (Observable Universe)

QUO-1: Non-degenerate integration on the Temperley--Lieb quotient

The Frobenius form \int_A induces A \cong A^{\vee}. At z = q^3/(q^2 + 1), the three-row antisymmetric weight y_{(1^3)} vanishes identically, so on the full Hecke algebra H_n(R, q) the Gram matrix G_{ij} = \mathrm{tr}_M(T_{\beta_i} \cdot T_{\beta_j}) satisfies \det G = 0 identically for every n \geq 3. Non-degenerate integration holds on the Temperley--Lieb quotient \mathrm{TL}_n(q) := H_n(R, q)/\mathrm{rad}\,\mathrm{tr}_M of dimension C_n:

  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\bar{x} \cdot \bar{y}\bigr)
  =  0
   \;\;\forall \bar{y} \in \mathrm{TL}_n(q)
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \bar{x} = 0  \text{ in } \mathrm{TL}_n(q),

equivalently \det G\big|_{\mathrm{TL}_n(q)} \neq 0 at generic q (while on H_n(R, q) itself \det G \neq 0 holds only for n \leq 2, where \mathrm{rad}\,\mathrm{tr}_M = 0).

QUO-2: Observability (\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0)

No braid word remains invariant under the adjoint (conjugation) action. In Hecke generators:

  \sigma_i w \sigma_i^{-1} =  w
  \quad \forall i
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  w \in R \cdot 1
   \text{(scalar multiple of the identity)}.

Equivalently: the only braid word commuting with all generators is the identity. In the vertex algebra, no nontrivial state a \in V satisfies Y(a, z) = \lambda\mathrm{id} for all z. Every state produces a genuinely z-dependent operator.

QUO-3: Measurability (anomaly freedom)

The second Chern class c_2(\mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 translates via the fibre functor to the relation QUO-3b below.

(QUO-3a) First Chern class obstruction. Representing c_1(\mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 by the naive antisymmetrised trace \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i - \sigma_i^{-1}) = 0 fails for every linear trace with \mathrm{tr}_M(1) \neq 0 when q^2 \neq 1. The Hecke relation QU-1a gives \sigma_i^{-1} = \sigma_i - (q - q^{-1}), so

  \sum_{i=1}^{n-1}
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\sigma_i - \sigma_i^{-1}\bigr)
  = (n-1)(q - q^{-1})\,\mathrm{tr}_M(1).

This is the skein relation L_+ - L_- = (q - q^{-1}) L_0 under the trace; it holds for every word and carries no information about c_1. A writhe-type functional that could express c_1(\mathrm{Ad}(A)) is not known in this framework.

(QUO-3b) Second Chern class vanishing (c_2 = 0):

  \sum_{i < j}
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(
    [\sigma_i, \sigma_j][\sigma_i, \sigma_j]^{\dagger}
  \bigr)
  =  0,

where [\sigma_i, \sigma_j] = \sigma_i \sigma_j - \sigma_j \sigma_i and \dagger is the anti-involution \sigma_i^{\dagger} = \sigma_i^{-1}. This prevents topological phases from accumulating under transport around the adjoint bundle.

QUO-4: Categorical volume constraint

The exterior power \Lambda^2 V maps onto \mathbf{1} via a non-degenerate epimorphism \epsilon preserved by gauge automorphisms. The antisymmetriser in H_2(R, q) is:

  \mathrm{Alt}_2
  = 
  \frac{1}{[2]_q}\bigl(\mathrm{id} - q^{-1} \sigma_1\bigr),
  \qquad
  [2]_q = q + q^{-1}.

The volume constraint reads:

  \epsilon \circ \mathrm{Alt}_2
  = 
  \epsilon
  \colon V^{\otimes 2} \to \mathbf{1},

and for every gauge automorphism g \in \mathrm{Aut}^{\otimes}(\tau):

  \epsilon \circ (\Lambda^2 g_V) =  \epsilon.

In Hecke generators, the antisymmetric contraction \epsilon satisfies:

  \epsilon\!\bigl(v \otimes w - q^{-1}(\sigma_1 \cdot v \otimes w)\bigr)
  = 
  [2]_q\epsilon(v \otimes w)

and is gauge-invariant, thereby fixing the q-deformed volume element.

Cohomological Constraints in Knot Coordinates

The QU/QUO axioms imply a suite of cohomological constraints. Each translates into a relation on braid words, Hecke generators, and the Markov trace.

C-1: De Rham complex (d^2 = 0 on horizontal forms)

The de Rham differential d\colon \Omega^k(A) \to \Omega^{k+1}(A) acts on modes via d(a_m z^{-m-1} dz) = a_{m-1} z^{-m} dz. In knot coordinates, the nilpotence d^2 = 0 on the horizontal subcomplex \Omega_H^k(A) becomes:

  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\Bigl(
    \check{R}_{(a)} z^{m-2}
  \Bigr)
  - 
  2\mathrm{tr}_M\!\Bigl(
    \check{R}_{(a)} z^{m-1}
  \Bigr)
  + 
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\Bigl(
    \check{R}_{(a)} z^{m}
  \Bigr)
  =  0

for all \xi-invariant states a. These are the states annihilated by the weight operator ([\xi, a] = 0), which correspond to braid words in the centre of H_n(R, q).

C-2: q-Deformed obstruction to nilpotence (d_q^2 \neq 0)

The q-exterior derivative d_q = q^{-1}d + (1 - q^{-1})\pi_V \circ d satisfies (categorical d_q^2):

  d_q^2\alpha
  = 
  q^{-1}(1 - q^{-1})\omega_V \wedge_q [\xi, \alpha].

In knot coordinates, the weight operator \xi acts on modes as the writhe grading:

  [\xi, a_m]
  = 
  \mathrm{wr}(a) a_m,

where \mathrm{wr}(a) is the writhe of \hat{\beta}_a: the exponent sum of the braid word \beta_a, i.e. its image under the abelianisation B_n \to \mathbb{Z}, \sigma_i^{\pm 1} \mapsto \pm 1. It is not a trace: the trace of \sum_i (\sigma_i - \sigma_i^{-1}) is the constant (n-1)(q - q^{-1})\mathrm{tr}_M(1) for every word.

The curvature 2-form \omega_V is the Hecke Casimir:

  \omega_V
  = 
  \sum_{i < j}
  (\sigma_i \sigma_j - \sigma_j \sigma_i) dz^i \wedge dz^j.

Thus d_q^2 = 0 if and only if q = 1 (classical limit) or \mathrm{wr}(\alpha) = 0 (horizontal forms). For generic q \neq 1 and non-horizontal \alpha, d_q^2 \neq 0: the q-deformed complex is not a cochain complex. The obstruction evaluates to writhe \times curvature.

C-3: Hodge star and Poincaré duality

The categorical Hodge star (categorical Hodge star) \star\colon \Omega^k(A) \to \Omega^{n-k}(A) satisfies \star^2 = \mathrm{id}. In knot coordinates, \star acts on modes via the antipode:

  \star(a_m)
  = 
  S(a_m)^*
  = 
  (\sigma_i^{-1})_m^*
  \qquad\text{where } (\cdot)^* \text{ is Frobenius conjugation.}

Poincaré duality in knot coordinates demands that for all braid words \beta, \beta':

  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(
    \rho(\beta) \cdot \star\rho(\beta')
  \bigr)
  = 
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(
    \rho(\beta) \cdot S(\rho(\beta'))^*
  \bigr)
  = 
  \delta_{\beta, \beta'} \mathrm{vol},

where \mathrm{vol} = \int_A(\mathrm{vol}) = 1 normalises the top form. The pairing is non-degenerate by QUO-1.

C-4: Euler characteristic constraint

The categorical Euler characteristic \chi(A) = \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_A) provides the rigidity trace. In knot coordinates, this evaluates to the Jones polynomial of the unknot at strand count n:

  \chi(A)
  = 
  \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathrm{id}_{H_n(R, q)})
  = 
  [n]_q!
  = 
  \prod_{k=1}^{n} \frac{q^k - q^{-k}}{q - q^{-1}}.

Stability under jet prolongation (C-4a):

  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\mathrm{id}_{J^1 H_n(R, q)}\bigr)
  = 
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\mathrm{id}_{H_n(R, q)}\bigr).

The translation operator L_{-1} preserves the Euler characteristic: \chi(A_{n+1}) = \chi(A_n) for all brane levels.

Descartes constraint (C-4b): For the physical universe,

  \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) =  -6
  \qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad
  \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathrm{id}) =  -6.

This forces genus g = 4 (Bring's surface), bounding the embeddable torus knots to the 7 generators \mathcal{G}.

C-5: obstruction classes

The quantum characteristic classes \kappa_n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B}) (quantum characteristic classes) obstruct lifting from brane level n to n+1. In knot variables, the failure of Markov stabilisation at the jet level detects this obstruction:

  \kappa_n
  = 
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(
    \check{R}_{(n+1)} - L_{-1} \check{R}_{(n)}
  \bigr)
   \in 
  H^2(\mathcal{S}_p, \mathcal{B}),

where \check{R}_{(n)} is the R-matrix at brane level n. The class \kappa_n = 0 if and only if jet prolongation determines the level-(n+1) braiding entirely from the level-n braiding.

Kummer persistence (C-5a): When \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6, item 3 of the QU-to-QOU theorem gives

  \kappa_n = 0 \iff n \mid 6,
  \qquad n \geq 1,

for the Kummer obstruction \chi(A) \bmod n. Asserting \kappa_n \neq 0 for all n via complementary subgroups for the jet corrections and the base obstruction does not go through globally. Whether the R-matrix expression defined above coincides with the Kummer obstruction is open, and only in a restricted sense can it hold. The Markov trace takes values in a torsion-free ring, and every additive map from \mathbb{Z}/n into a torsion-free group is zero. So the trace expression cannot be the image of the Kummer class under any homomorphism; at most it can vanish at the same levels n \mid 6. It is also identically zero whenever \check{R}_{(n+1)} is the jet image of \check{R}_{(n)}, as it is for \check{R} = \sigma_i at every level. What does hold at the level of traces is the identity route: by C-4b, \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathrm{id}) = \chi(A) = -6, so the Kummer obstruction at level n is \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathrm{id}) \bmod n.

Scope. Item 3 of QU-to-QOU establishes persistence in the Kummer tower (the obstruction \chi(\mathcal{S}) \bmod n to an n-th root of the Reeb bundle), rather than at every level of the jet tower. On a closed surface such as Bring's surface, the complementary-subgroup step does not hold for the bands considered here: H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{S}}) = 0, so the jet corrections \delta_n vanish; for the band \mathbb{Z}, the group H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathbb{Z} has no non-trivial complement; and for \mathcal{O}^{\times} and \mathbb{G}_m, the obstruction group itself is zero. C-6: Betti numbers and spectral sequence

The Leray--Serre spectral sequence controls the Betti numbers b_k = \dim H^k(\mathcal{S}_n, \mathbb{R}). In knot variables, b_k counts linearly independent k-fold products of Hecke generators modulo the de Rham relation:

  b_k(\mathcal{S}_n)
  = 
  \dim_R
  \frac{
    \ker\!\bigl(d\colon \Omega^k_{H_n(R, q)} \to \Omega^{k+1}_{H_n(R, q)}\bigr)
  }{
    \mathrm{im}\!\bigl(d\colon \Omega^{k-1}_{H_n(R, q)} \to \Omega^k_{H_n(R, q)}\bigr)
  },

where \Omega^k_{H_n(R, q)} is the space of degree-k antisymmetric Hecke words:

  \Omega^k_{H_n(R, q)}
  = 
  \mathrm{span}\!\bigl\{
    T_{i_1} T_{i_2} \cdots T_{i_k}
     \big| 
    i_1 < i_2 < \cdots < i_k
  \bigr\} \cdot \mathrm{Alt}_k,

with \mathrm{Alt}_k = \sum_{\pi \in S_k} \mathrm{sgn}(\pi) q^{-\ell(\pi)} T_\pi the q-antisymmetriser.

C-7: Instanton constraint (self-dual curvature)

The categorical instanton condition \star_q F_\nabla = F_\nabla (instanton on-shell) becomes a relation on the curvature 2-form in Hecke generators. The curvature F_\nabla = \nabla^2 has components:

  (F_\nabla)_{ij}

  \sum_k f^k_{ij} \sigma_k,

where f^k_{ij} are the structure constants of the Iwahori--Hecke algebra. The self-duality equation reads:

  \star_q (F_\nabla)_{ij}
  = 
  (F_\nabla)_{ij}
  \qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad
  S\!\bigl([\sigma_i, \sigma_j]\bigr)^*
  = 
  [\sigma_i, \sigma_j].

The curvature is invariant under the combined antipode-conjugation. It is self-adjoint in the Frobenius inner product.

Bogomolny bound (C-7a): The instanton number equals c_2(A):

  \lVert F_\nabla \rVert^2
  = 
  \sum_{i < j}
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(
    [\sigma_i, \sigma_j] \cdot [\sigma_i, \sigma_j]^{\dagger}
  \bigr)
  = 
  c_2(A).

By QUO-3b this vanishes for the adjoint. The adjoint bundle is flat. For the fundamental representation, c_2(A) supplies the topological charge (knot crossing number modulo signs).

C-8: Hodge--Laplacian and harmonic braid words

The q-Laplacian \Delta_q = d_q \delta_q + \delta_q d_q (Hodge--Laplacian) is self-adjoint. In knot coordinates:

  \Delta_q
  = 
  q^{-2}\Delta
  + 
  q^{-1}(1 - q^{-1})\bigl(
    \omega_V \wedge_q \iota_\xi
    + 
    \iota_\xi \omega_V \wedge_q

where \Delta = d\delta + \delta d is the undeformed Laplacian and \iota_\xi is contraction with the weight vector.

Harmonic states are braid words \beta satisfying \Delta_q \rho(\beta) = 0. In Hecke generators:

  \Delta_q \sigma_\beta = 0
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  d_q\sigma_\beta = 0
   \text{and} 
  \delta_q \sigma_\beta = 0.

The space \ker \Delta_q constitutes the particle state space. Its dimension equals the number of linearly independent knot-particles at each brane level. Over K = \mathbb{R}, it acquires the Hilbert structure of \ker \Delta_q \subset L^2(A); over a general field, it is a finite-dimensional vector space.

The cohomology of the moduli surface \Sigma_g (cohomological embedding) admits a knot basis. In knot coordinates, each cohomology generator corresponds to a specific Hecke word:

  H^*(\Sigma_4)
  = 
  \mathrm{span}\!\bigl\{
    1,
    T_{(2,3)},
    T_{(2,5)},
    T_{(2,7)},
    T_{(3,5)},
    T_{(2,9)},
    T_{(3,4)},
    T_{(4_1)},
    T_{(4_1)}^*,
    \mathrm{vol}
  \bigr\},

where T_{(m,n)} = \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\sigma^{(m,n)})) evaluates the torus knot braid word \sigma^{(m,n)} \in B_m via the Markov trace.

C-10: \v{C}ech--Yekutieli descent cocycle

The cosimplicial crossed groupoid structure on the brane tower provides a \v{C}ech cocycle condition at each level. In knot variables, the twisted 2-cocycle is:

  d\!\bigl(g^{(n)}_{ijk}\bigr)
  = 
  a^{(n)}_{ij} \cdot g^{(n)}_{ijk} \cdot
  \bigl(a^{(n)}_{jk}\bigr)^{-1},

where g^{(n)}_{ijk} \in H_n(R, q) is the transition braid word on triple overlaps and a^{(n)}_{ij} are 2-morphism braid words. In Hecke generators, the cocycle condition translates to:

  T_{a_{ij}} \cdot T_{g_{ikl}} \cdot T_{a_{kl}}^{-1}
  \qquad\text{(in \(H_n(R, q)\))},

where T_g = \rho(g) denotes the Hecke image of a braid word. This is the gluing condition for locally defined braid words to patch into a global knot invariant.

Proposition QU/QUO and cohomological relations on the jet bundle. Every relation in the QU/QUO presentation (vertex algebra relations) lifts to the jet bundle J^n(A) = A_n via the brane tower (recursive brane tower). The jet prolongation L_{-1}\colon A_n \to A_{n+1} promotes each level-n Iwahori--Hecke algebra H^{(n)}(q) to a level-(n{+}1) Hecke algebra H^{(n+1)}(q). Write \sigma_i^{(n)} for the Hecke generators, \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)} for the level-n Markov trace, and \check{R}^{(n)} for the level-n R-matrix; the jet embedding \ell_n and the descent \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} satisfy

  \ell_n(\sigma_i^{(n)}) = \sigma_i^{(n+1)}, \qquad
  \mathfrak{d}_{n+1}\colon H^{(n+1)}(q) \to H^{(n)}(q), \qquad
  \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} \circ \ell_n = \mathrm{id}.

The descent involution \hat{\tau}_n = \ell_n \circ \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} splits the level-(n{+}1) relations into descended (inherited from level n) and transient (genuinely new at level n{+}1). The presentation on J^n(A) comprises 24 relations — 11 structural (level-n lifts of QU/QUO), 4 descent, and 9 cohomological, two of the structural eleven (J-3c and J-4a) being the inter-level relations that bind adjacent brane levels — catalogued in Table 1, Table 2, and Table 3.

Proof

The relations are exhibited level by level.

I. Structural relations on J^n(A)

J-1: Hecke relations (level n)

The Hecke generators at every brane level satisfy the identical quadratic, braid, and locality relations:

(J-1a) \sigma_i^{(n)2} = (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i^{(n)} + 1

(J-1b) \sigma_i^{(n)} \sigma_{i+1}^{(n)} \sigma_i^{(n)} = \sigma_{i+1}^{(n)} \sigma_i^{(n)} \sigma_{i+1}^{(n)}

(J-1c) \sigma_i^{(n)} \sigma_j^{(n)} = \sigma_j^{(n)} \sigma_i^{(n)} \qquad (|i - j| \geq 2)

The aether parameter q is the same at every level. This manifests the Euler characteristic stability \chi(A_n) = \chi(A_0).

J-2: Jet-prolonged Frobenius--Hopf relations

The multiplication \mu_n, comultiplication \Delta_n, and antipode S_n on A_n inherit from A_0 by jet prolongation. The Frobenius relation lifts level by level:

(J-2a) Frobenius sliding at level n:

  (\mu_n \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ
  (\mathrm{id} \otimes \Delta_n)
  = 
  \Delta_n \circ \mu_n.

In knot coordinates:

  \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}\!\bigl(
    \rho_n(\beta_1) \cdot \rho_n(\beta_2 \cdot \beta_3)
  \bigr)
  = 
  \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}\!\bigl(
    \rho_n(\beta_1 \cdot \beta_2) \cdot \rho_n(\beta_3)
  \bigr).

(J-2b) Antipode at level n: S_n(\sigma_i^{(n)}) = \sigma_i^{(n)-1} = \sigma_i^{(n)} - (q - q^{-1}).

(J-2c) Level-n Frobenius pairing:

  \langle a, b \rangle_n
  = 
  \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}\!\bigl(
    \rho_n(\hat{\beta}_a \cdot \hat{\beta}_b)
  \bigr).

At the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2 + 1), \det G^{(n)} = 0 identically on the full m-strand Hecke algebra H_m^{(n)}(q) for m \geq 3 (the Young diagrams with at least three rows forming \mathrm{rad}\,\mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}); non-degeneracy holds on the level-n Temperley--Lieb quotient \mathrm{TL}_m^{(n)}(q) := H_m^{(n)}(q)/\mathrm{rad}\,\mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)} of dimension C_m, where \det G^{(n)}\big|_{\mathrm{TL}_m^{(n)}(q)} \neq 0 at every brane level.

J-3: Markov trace at level n

(J-3a) Conjugation invariance:

  \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(\sigma_i^{(n)} \cdot w)
  = 
  \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(w \cdot \sigma_i^{(n)})
  \qquad \forall w \in H^{(n)}(q).

(J-3b) Stabilisation:

  \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(w \cdot \sigma_m^{(n)})
  = 
  z\,\mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(w),
  \qquad
  \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(w \cdot \sigma_m^{(n)-1})
  = 
  z_-\,\mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(w),

with z = \dfrac{q^3}{q^2 + 1} and z_- = \dfrac{1}{q(q^2 + 1)}.

(J-3c) Inter-level compatibility (jet prolongation preserves the Markov trace):

  \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n+1)}\!\bigl(\ell_n(w)\bigr)
  = 
  \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(w)
  \qquad \forall w \in H^{(n)}(q).

This acts as the knot-variable form of Euler stability: the Jones polynomial of a knot remains independent of brane level.

J-4: Translation operator between levels

(J-4a) Mode relation across levels:

  [L_{-1}, a_m^{(n)}] =  -m a_{m-1}^{(n+1)},

where a_m^{(n)} = \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(\check{R}^{(n)}_{(a)} z^m) represents the m-th mode at level n. The commutator maps level-n modes to level-(n{+}1) modes. The translation operator operates as the inter-level ladder.

(J-4b) Vacuum stability across levels:

  |0\rangle^{(n)} =  \ell_{n-1} \circ \cdots \circ \ell_0(|0\rangle)
  =  1 \in A_n.

The unknot embeds identically at every level.

J-5: Observability at level n

  \sigma_i^{(n)} w \sigma_i^{(n)-1} = w
   \forall i
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  w \in R \cdot 1  \text{in } H^{(n)}(q).

The vanishing of \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A_n)) propagates from level 0 via jet prolongation: any \mathrm{Ad}-invariant at level n{+}1 projects to one at level n, contradicting the base case.

J-6: Volume constraint at level n

  \epsilon_n \circ \mathrm{Alt}_2^{(n)} =  \epsilon_n,
  \qquad
  \epsilon_n \circ (\Lambda^2 g_V^{(n)}) = \epsilon_n.

The q-antisymmetriser \mathrm{Alt}_2^{(n)} = \frac{1}{[2]_q}(\mathrm{id} - q^{-1} \sigma_1^{(n)}) adopts the same form at every level (same q). The volume constraint is thus level-independent.

II. Descent decomposition of relations

The descent involution \hat{\tau}_n = \ell_n \circ \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} operates idempotently on H^{(n+1)}(q) and splits every relation into descended and transient parts.

D-1: Descended Hecke generators

  \hat{\tau}_n(\sigma_i^{(n+1)})
  = 
  \ell_n\!\bigl(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}(\sigma_i^{(n+1)})\bigr)
  = 
  \ell_n(\sigma_i^{(n)})
  = 
  \sigma_i^{(n+1)}.

For i \leq n-1: the base Hecke generators are entirely descended. They signify the exact same crossing at every level. The Hecke relation QU-1a is purely descended.

D-2: Transient generators

At level n{+}1, the jet prolongation may produce new generators \sigma^{(n+1)}_{\mathrm{new}} in the transient complement \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{trans}}_{n+1} = \ker\hat{\tau}_n. These satisfy:

  \hat{\tau}_n(\sigma^{(n+1)}_{\mathrm{new}}) =  0,
  \qquad
  \mathfrak{d}_{n+1}(\sigma^{(n+1)}_{\mathrm{new}}) =  0.

Transient generators lack a pre-image at level n. They obey the Hecke relation (J-1a) at level n{+}1 but their Markov traces are invisible at level n:

  \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}\!\bigl(
    \mathfrak{d}_{n+1}(\sigma^{(n+1)}_{\mathrm{new}})
  \bigr)
  =  0.

D-3: Descent of the Frobenius relation

The Frobenius sliding relation (J-2a) decomposes as:

  \Delta_n \circ \mu_n
  = 
  \underbrace{
    \hat{\tau}_n(\Delta_{n+1} \circ \mu_{n+1})
  }_{\text{descended (from level \(n\))}}
  + 
  \underbrace{
    (1 - \hat{\tau}_n)(\Delta_{n+1} \circ \mu_{n+1})
  }_{\text{transient correction}}.

The transient correction captures the jet curvature: the failure of the level-(n{+}1) Frobenius relation to be entirely governed by level n.

D-4: Bosonic vs fermionic modes

The descent eigenspaces (descent eigenspaces) partition modes by statistics:

  • Bosonic (longitudinal): w \in \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{desc}}_{n+1} obeys \hat{\tau}_n(w) = w. In knot coordinates: braid words whose Markov trace is fully fixed at level n:
  \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n+1)}(w) =  \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}(w)).
  • Fermionic (ladder): w \in \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{trans}}_{n+1} obeys \hat{\tau}_n(w) = 0. In knot coordinates: braid words whose Markov trace vanishes when descended:
  \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}(w)) =  0.

Fermionic modes are the jet-created braid words without an analogue at the prior level.

JC-1: De Rham complex at level n

  d_n^2 =  0
  \qquad\text{on } \Omega^k_H(A_n),

where \Omega^k_H(A_n) signifies the horizontal subcomplex at level n (braid words with zero writhe at level n).

  d_{q,n}^2\alpha
  =

JC-3: Euler characteristic stability

  \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(\mathrm{id}_{H^{(n)}(q)})

where c_2^{\mathrm{desc}} = c_2(A_{n-1}) is descended and c_2^{\mathrm{trans}} constitutes the topological charge of the transient sector.

A categorical transfer matrix for \mathfrak{H}_p is the equivalence class

  \mathcal{T}(\mathfrak{H})
  = 
  \bigl[ T \bigr]_{\sim}
   \in 
  \mathrm{End}\bigl(H_n(R, q)\bigr) \big/ \sim

where T is any braiding operation on \mathfrak{H} (at either level) and the equivalence relation \sim identifies two operations T_1 \sim T_2 whenever they produce the same vertex volume:

  T_1 \sim T_2
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  \hat{V}(T_1, q) = \hat{V}(T_2, q)

prop:transfer-matrix-level-independence:
Proposition Transfer matrix level independence. Conditional on Hecke normal forms realise crystal highest-weight vectors. Let \mathfrak{H}_p = [K_1, \ldots, K_n]_p \oplus \mathcal{L} be a hadron with composite knot K_{\mathfrak{H}} = \hat{\beta}_{\mathfrak{H}}. Let \mathcal{T}(\mathfrak{H}_p) be the categorical transfer matrix (categorical transfer matrix). Then:

  1. Constituent-composite agreement. The composite invariant is derived from the constituents rather than independent of them: the Markov trace computed from the constituent insertion points (z_1, \ldots, z_n) is the composite invariant, so two hadrons with the same constituents have the same composite. Concretely,

      \prod_{i=0}^{n-2} \hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{const}}(q)
  = 
  \hat{V}^{\mathrm{comp}}(q)
  = 
  J_{K_{\mathfrak{H}}}(q).

  2. Path independence on \mathcal{S}_p. Two braiding operations T_1, T_2 on \mathfrak{H} that produce isotopy-equivalent configurations have the same categorical transfer matrix: \mathcal{T}(T_1) = \mathcal{T}(T_2). In particular, the specific sequence of crossing changes within the exceptional divisor \mathcal{S}_p does not affect the result --- only the equivalence class of the final configuration matters.

  3. Well-definedness. The categorical transfer matrix \mathcal{T}(\mathfrak{H}) depends only on the isotopy class of the hadron \mathfrak{H} and the knot types K_i of its constituents. It is independent of:

    • the braid representative \beta_{\mathfrak{H}},
    • the PawLei embedding \iota_{j_i} for each constituent,
    • the order of crossings evaluated within \mathcal{S}_p.

Conjecture Topological mass formula (Archimedean). Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be the \mathbb{C}-quantum observable universe and let K be a hyperbolic knot whose complement carries the vortex topology of a stable particle, generated by N blow-ups along the brane tower. It is conjectured that the mass formula

  \mathfrak{m}(K) = \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(K)}{\hbar_q^{2}}

holds, where \mathrm{Vol}(K) is the hyperbolic volume of S^3 \setminus K and \hbar_q = 1 - 1/q is the quantum Planck constant (quantum Planck constant) at the aether parameter q (aether parameter). The archimedean-realisation framing of this closed form is described in the topological mass-formula context.

Derivation sketch

The derivation assumes the categorical decomposition (topological mass), which is itself a conjecture, and then makes three identifications through the archimedean bridge. Step 2 takes an identity as a hypothesis. Only Step 3 is proved.

Step 1 — baseline holonomy \mapsto hyperbolic volume. The descended trace of the universal vortex \varrho_0 is the holonomy norm \lVert \mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A}(\varrho_0; \mathfrak{G}) \rVert. Under the archimedean fibre functor (categorical-archimedean-bridge) this is the imaginary part of the Chern--Simons functional on the flat connection associated to K, which by the Chern–Simons / hyperbolic-volume correspondence equals \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K) (Möbius energy). Concretely,

  \mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{tr}\bigl(\hat{\tau}_n^{\mathrm{desc}}\,\mathrm{Hol}\bigr)
  \;=\; \mathrm{Vol}(K).

Step 2 — transient dilogarithm sum \mapsto (1/\hbar_q^{2} - 1) correction. The transient eigenspace contributes one quantum-dilogarithm factor \Phi_q(z_i) per blow-up exceptional divisor. In the Briggs–Klein spectral coordinates of the brane tower (mass-endomorphism on the jet tower), the z_i are the eigenvalues of the per-crossing transfer operator on the curvature-rank stratification. Summing over the N blow-ups and using the dilogarithm identity \sum_{i=1}^N \Phi_q(z_i) = (1/\hbar_q^{2} - 1)\,\mathrm{Vol}(K) (Kashaev–Murakami volume conjecture restricted to the q-deformation; this is the dilogarithm-evaluation hypothesis of the archimedean mass formula):

  \sum_{i=1}^{N} \Phi_q(z_i)
  \;=\; \mathrm{Vol}(K)\bigl(\hbar_q^{-2} - 1\bigr).

This identity is a hypothesis on the archimedean structure rather than a derived theorem; the evaluation in Briggs–Klein coordinates is the categorical content the formula imports from the geometric side.

Step 3 — combine. Adding the baseline and transient contributions and recognising 1 + (\hbar_q^{-2} - 1) = \hbar_q^{-2}:

  \mathfrak{m}(K)
  \;=\; \mathrm{Vol}(K) + \mathrm{Vol}(K)\bigl(\hbar_q^{-2} - 1\bigr)
  \;=\; \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(K)}{\hbar_q^{2}}.

def:hecke-mass-element:
Definition Hecke mass element. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with Hecke algebra H_n(R, q) (Hecke algebra) and Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M \colon H_n(R, q) \to k (Jones--Markov trace).

Let \varrho \colon \mathbf{1} \to A be a vortex morphism with braid representative \beta \in B_n. The mass integrand (mass identity) is the composition

  \alpha_\varrho
  =
  (\textstyle\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id})
  \circ \Delta
  \circ \varrho
  \colon \mathbf{1} \to A,

and L_{\alpha_\varrho} \in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A) is left multiplication by \alpha_\varrho in the Frobenius--Hopf algebra A.

The Hecke mass element of the vortex \varrho is

  \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta)
  \;:=\;
  \tau\bigl(L_{\alpha_\varrho}\bigr)
  \;\in\; H_n(R, q).

Its descended and transient parts are

  \Phi^{\mathrm{desc}}(\beta) := \tau\bigl(\hat{\tau}_n(L_{\alpha_\varrho})\bigr),
  \qquad
  \Phi^{\mathrm{trans}}(\beta) := \tau\bigl(L_{\alpha_\varrho} - \hat{\tau}_n(L_{\alpha_\varrho})\bigr),

where \hat{\tau}_n is the descent involution (descent eigenspaces).

By quantum Schur--Weyl duality, every such endomorphism is an element of the Hecke algebra, so the Hecke mass element lies in H_n(R, q).

The descent involution \hat{\tau}_n induces an idempotent decomposition \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta) = \Phi^{\mathrm{desc}}(\beta) + \Phi^{\mathrm{trans}}(\beta) within H_n(R, q): \Phi^{\mathrm{desc}} encodes the base-level (descended) cycle and \Phi^{\mathrm{trans}} encodes the transient contributions at the blow-up centres.

prop:hecke-generator-poly-reduction:
Proposition Single-generator Hecke polynomial reduction. Let \sigma_i be a Hecke generator, satisfying the quadratic relation \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\,\sigma_i + 1. For any finite list of scalars d_1, \dots, d_r \in R, the product of single-generator factors collapses to an R-linear combination of \sigma_i and the identity,

  \prod_{j=1}^{r} \bigl(\sigma_i + d_j\,1\bigr) \;=\; \alpha\,\sigma_i + \beta\,1,

where (\alpha, \beta) is given by the division-free recursion

  (\alpha,\beta)_{\varnothing} = (0,\,1),
  \qquad
  (\alpha,\beta)_{d\,::\,\mathrm{ds}}
    = \bigl(\alpha'\,(h + d) + \beta',\;\; \alpha' + \beta'\,d\bigr),

with h = q - q^{-1} and (\alpha',\beta') the coefficients for the tail \mathrm{ds}.

Consequence for the Markov trace

In a seminormal (Gelfand–Zetlin) representation the diagonal entry of \alpha\,\sigma_i + \beta\,1 on a two-box block depends only on the content gap \delta' of the two boxes added at that step, through the eigenvalue D(\delta') of \sigma_i. Hence whenever a braid word has a monotone generator sequence — as the multi-nucleon atom word \beta_{\mathrm{atom}} does, each nucleon contributing \sigma_{3k}, \sigma_{3k+1} and one interface crossing \sigma_{3k+2} without revisiting a generator — every per-generator operator O_g is a single-generator polynomial, and its seminormal diagonal is a single \alpha_g\,D(\delta'_g) + \beta_g. The character then factorises as a sum over Bratteli chains of a product of such local factors:

  \chi^\lambda(\beta_{\mathrm{atom}})
   = \sum_{\varnothing = s_0 \subset s_1 \subset \cdots \subset s_n = \lambda}
       \ \prod_g \bigl(\alpha_g\,D(\delta'_g) + \beta_g\bigr),

a transfer matrix over the Young lattice that never materialises the d_\lambda-dimensional Hoefsmit representation. This is the mechanism by which the canonical Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda\,\chi^\lambda scales to large atoms (Steps 3 and 9b of the mass–binding chain): the per-block work drops to a few field operations, removing the n! wall of the per-basis-vector evaluation.
prf:hecke-generator-poly-reduction:
Proof Proof of hecke generator poly reduction. By induction on the list. The empty product is 1 = 0\cdot\sigma_i + 1\cdot 1. For the step, suppose \prod_{\mathrm{ds}} = \alpha'\,\sigma_i + \beta'\,1. Then

\begin{aligned}
(\sigma_i + d\,1)\,(\alpha'\,\sigma_i + \beta'\,1)
  &= \alpha'\,\sigma_i^2 + (\beta' + d\,\alpha')\,\sigma_i + d\,\beta'\,1 \\
  &= \alpha'\,\bigl((q-q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1\bigr) + (\beta' + d\,\alpha')\,\sigma_i + d\,\beta'\,1 \\
  &= \bigl(\alpha'(h + d) + \beta'\bigr)\,\sigma_i + \bigl(\alpha' + \beta'\,d\bigr)\,1,
\end{aligned}

using the quadratic relation in the second line. This is exactly (\alpha,\beta)_{d\,::\,\mathrm{ds}}. \qquad\blacksquare

This is the Cayley–Hamilton reduction for the rank-one quadratic that every Hecke generator satisfies: since \sigma_i annihilates (x - q)(x + q^{-1}), any polynomial in \sigma_i alone is congruent to a linear remainder \alpha\,\sigma_i + \beta\,1 modulo that quadratic. The recursion is purely ring-theoretic, holding over any commutative base ring R with no archimedean or invertibility hypothesis. (The closed eigenvalue form \alpha = (E_1 - E_2)/(q + q^{-1}), E_1 = \prod_j (q + d_j), E_2 = \prod_j (-q^{-1} + d_j) used for canonical speed is a corollary that does require q + q^{-1} to be invertible.)

Statement

The descent involution \hat\tau_n at the first brane level projects onto the H_1(q) content of H_3(R, q).
